data.cultural_impact: The name Shahrokh is of Persian origin and holds a significant cultural impact in the Islamic world due to its regal and noble meaning. Historically, the name was borne by various rulers and warriors throughout Middle Eastern history, inspiring a sense of awe and respect. Today, the name is cherished in many Muslim communities as a symbol of strength, power, and nobility.
data.spiritual_significance: In the Islamic tradition, the name Shahrokh carries a deep spiritual significance representing the notion of God's divine power and sovereignty over the universe. It serves as a reminder that ultimate control and power belong to Allah, and that all human rulers and leaders are merely His vicegerents on Earth. The name also evokes the character traits of wisdom, justice, and compassion, which are highly regarded qualities in the Islamic faith.

historical_references.reference: Shahrokh I, also known as Shahrukh Mirza, was a Timurid ruler who reigned from 1405 to 1447. He was the son of Miranshah and succeeded his father upon his death. Shahrokh expanded his territories and ruled over parts of present-day India, Iran, and Central Asia. He is known for his military campaigns and architectural achievements.

Shahrokh II, also known as Shahrukh Mirza Sur, was a Sayyid ruler who reigned from 1501 to 1542. He was the founder of the Sur Dynasty in Gujarat, India. Shahrokh II conquered the region from the Kathiawad Sultanate and established the capital city of Ahmedabad. He is known for his patronage of arts, literature, and architecture.
